author: show-me state times
title: Workers' Compensation Law Committee emphasizes education opportunities for lawyers, public
text:
The Workers’ Compensation Law Committee is highlighting on Apr. 29 its efforts to provide educational resources and networking opportunities for lawyers handling workers’ compensation claims.
The committee aims to support legal professionals by offering case law updates, programs with medical experts, and practical guidance in the field of workers’ compensation. Chair Da-Niel Cunningham said, “I’ve had a great time being an active participant of the work comp committee. I encourage other members of The Missouri Bar to do the same (and join a committee).”
Cunningham said that committees help lawyers connect with peers in similar areas of law and allow them to give back to their communities and profession. The Workers’ Compensation Law Committee has nearly 600 members and regularly provides education and training both for attorneys and the public. Recent projects include developing a workers’ compensation FAQ page on ShowMeRights.org as well as creating resources for the Work Comp Connect online claims portal managed by the Missouri Division of Workers’ Compensation.
Continuing legal education remains a priority for the group, which is offering a free virtual session on technology’s role in improving legal practice systems during Spring Committee Meetings at 11 a.m. on Thursday, April 30. Christina Sondermann Capizzi, a St. Louis lawyer, will lead this session focused on modernizing workflow not only for workers’ compensation practitioners but all attorneys.
Committee members also participate in events such as the annual Workers’ Compensation Institute; this year’s program was held in person April 17 and will be available online May 4.
The Missouri Bar serves all practicing attorneys across Missouri as an integrated professional association according to its official website. It offers continuing education resources, publications, public tools like lawyer directories, partnerships with educators to promote legal awareness, and operates from headquarters in Jefferson City under direction from an elected Board of Governors according to its official website. The organization contributes by providing legal information resources that bolster justice throughout Missouri according to its official website.
